Live evidence for perles-net-k3j.2 (spike S2+S4), captured 2026-08-23 against
codex-cli 0.149.0. Scratch `notify` program set in ~/.codex/config.toml
during the spike, restored byte-identical afterward (verified by diff and
sha256sum in the findings comment).

Setup: notify program is a dedup ledger keyed on a SIMULATED mailbox
message-id (env NITRO_SPIKE_SIM_MSG_ID, default "SIM-MSG-1", constant across
turns of the same run), modeling the plan's real per-message-id
session_deliveries ledger. On each notify invocation it parses `thread-id`
from the payload, and if SIM-MSG-1 has not yet been "delivered" it claims it
(writes a ledger file) and runs `codex queue --thread <thread-id> --message
"Digest: 1 unread message SIM-MSG-1. Reply with exactly:
DIGEST_DELIVERED_SIM-MSG-1 (do not call tools)."`; otherwise it logs a skip
and does nothing.

=== Turn 1: fresh `codex exec` ===

Command: codex exec --json --skip-git-repo-check -o t1-out.txt "Say exactly:
TURN_ONE. Do not call any tools." (cwd = scratch run2 dir)

Stream: {"type":"thread.started","thread_id":"01a02e55-0354-7942-9279-84923a395f9c"}
... {"item":{"type":"agent_message","text":"TURN_ONE"}} ... turn.completed.
Process EXIT=0 (codex exec always fully exits after its one turn; confirmed
by `ps aux` showing no surviving process for the thread and by bash seeing
the exit code before notify's own log entries were even inspected).

notify-msgid.log:
  === notify-capture-msgid invoked at 2026-08-23T13:15:22,522658708+02:00 pid=1712385 (call #1) ===
  thread-id=01a02e55-0354-7942-9279-84923a395f9c
  LEDGER(msgid): SIM-MSG-1 not yet delivered -- claiming and queueing (call #1)
  QUEUE rc=0 out=Queued message 01a02e55-1411-7501-9205-9e155258a045 for thread 01a02e55-0354-7942-9279-84923a395f9c.
  === notify-capture-msgid exiting at 2026-08-23T13:15:22,823306110+02:00 (call #1) ===

Wall time inside the notify handler for the queue call: ~301ms
(13:15:22.522 receipt -> 13:15:22.823 exit). This happened AFTER the codex
exec process that produced turn 1 had already exited (task_complete was
written to the rollout before notify fired; the exec process's own exit
code was already observable by the shell). So "queue from inside notify
against the just-completed thread" does NOT re-enter a still-live process
for the codex-exec harness: there is no live process left to re-enter by the
time notify runs. `codex queue` instead writes into a durable, cross-process
SQLite table (~/.codex/queue_1.sqlite, table queued_items, PK id, columns
thread_id/payload_json/queue_order/created_at_ms/updated_at_ms), decoupled
from any running process:

  sqlite3 -readonly ~/.codex/queue_1.sqlite \
    "SELECT id, thread_id FROM queued_items WHERE thread_id='01a02e55-0354-7942-9279-84923a395f9c';"
  -> 01a02e55-1411-7501-9205-9e155258a045|01a02e55-0354-7942-9279-84923a395f9c

=== Turn 2: resume the SAME thread with a new prompt (models "queued turn start") ===

Command: codex exec --json --skip-git-repo-check -o t2-out.txt resume
01a02e55-0354-7942-9279-84923a395f9c "Say exactly: TURN_TWO."

Stream:
  {"type":"thread.started","thread_id":"01a02e55-0354-7942-9279-84923a395f9c"}
  {"type":"turn.started"}
  {"item":{"type":"agent_message","text":"DIGEST_DELIVERED_SIM-MSG-1"}}
  {"item":{"type":"agent_message","text":"TURN_TWO"}}
  {"type":"turn.completed", ...}

Rollout transcript for this turn (single turn_id
01a02e55-163f-7f90-ba1c-17d0bc5ccf49) shows the queued digest delivered as
its OWN user-message item, injected BEFORE the new resume prompt, both
processed within the SAME turn:

  EVENT task_started 01a02e55-163f-7f90-ba1c-17d0bc5ccf49
  user | Digest: 1 unread message SIM-MSG-1. Reply with exactly: DIGEST_DELIVERED_SIM-MSG-1 (do not call tools).
  assistant | DIGEST_DELIVERED_SIM-MSG-1
  user | Say exactly: TURN_TWO.
  assistant | TURN_TWO
  EVENT task_complete 01a02e55-163f-7f90-ba1c-17d0bc5ccf49

Key finding: a queued message does NOT start its own separate turn. It is
prepended as an extra user-message item ahead of whatever the next actual
turn's prompt is, and that combined turn produces exactly one
agent-turn-complete notify firing (one turn_id, one notify call). There is
no way observed in this spike to make `codex exec resume <thread>` drain the
queue with NO new prompt at all: `codex exec resume <thread>` with no prompt
argument and no stdin errors "No prompt provided via stdin." (exit 1) rather
than silently flushing the queue. Draining the queue requires something
external to supply the next real turn (a resume with a prompt, or, for a
persistent/interactive session, its own next natural input) -- consistent
with the plan's "next turn boundary" framing (mail-notify-plan.md:323), not
an instantaneous same-process re-entry.

=== Turn 2's completion re-fires notify: loop-guard proof ===

notify-msgid.log (continued):
  === notify-capture-msgid invoked at 2026-08-23T13:15:28,809579332+02:00 pid=1713940 (call #2) ===
  thread-id=01a02e55-0354-7942-9279-84923a395f9c
  LEDGER(msgid): SIM-MSG-1 already delivered at 2026-08-23T13:15:22,533512746+02:00 -- NOT queueing (loop guard fired, call #2)
  === notify-capture-msgid exiting at 2026-08-23T13:15:28,825449190+02:00 (call #2) ===

Confirmed: turn 2's completion DID re-fire notify (call #2, same thread-id).
The ledger found SIM-MSG-1 already delivered and skipped queueing. The
queue table for this thread is empty after turn 2:

  sqlite3 -readonly ~/.codex/queue_1.sqlite \
    "SELECT id, thread_id FROM queued_items WHERE thread_id='01a02e55-0354-7942-9279-84923a395f9c';"
  -> (no rows)

This is the single captured end-to-end trace demonstrating no infinite
notify loop when a dedup guard (keyed on the delivered mail message-id, not
on turn-id) skips already-delivered messages: two notify firings, one queue
call, zero queue calls on the second firing, loop terminates.

=== Separate run: what happens WITHOUT a message-id-scoped guard ===

An earlier run (separate scratch handler keyed on (thread-id, turn-id)
instead of message-id -- i.e. NOT modeling the real ledger) queued a new
marker on every notify firing (each turn has a unique turn-id), which would
grow unbounded if something kept auto-resuming the thread. This confirms the
loop's termination in production depends entirely on the ledger being keyed
by delivered mail message-id (as the plan specifies for session_deliveries),
not by turn/session identity; a turn-id-keyed guard does not terminate the
loop by itself. Log (notify.log), thread 01a02e51-c257-75c3-b242-b56199a18839:

  call #1 turn-id=01a02e51-c2d5-7931-9b5b-b7da941a16dc -> queued
  call #2 turn-id=01a02e53-e701-7cd3-bc87-32a25069a781 -> queued (different turn-id, guard did not fire)

=== Foreign-notify chaining timing (turn 1's handler) ===

The turn-1 handler execed a fake pre-existing "foreign" notify script after
its own work, preserving argv (matching the plan's wrapper design: "ours
execs it after our work, preserving argv/stdin/cwd/exit code"):

  notify.log: chaining to foreign notify at 2026-08-23T13:11:50,363526290+02:00
  foreign-notify.log: === foreign-notify invoked at 2026-08-23T13:11:50,368560355+02:00 pid=1692227 ===
    argc=1
    arg: {"type":"agent-turn-complete","thread-id":"01a02e51-c257-75c3-b242-b56199a18839", ...}
  foreign-notify.log: === foreign-notify exiting at 2026-08-23T13:11:50,371438320+02:00 ===
  notify.log: foreign notify done at 2026-08-23T13:11:50,377499413+02:00 rc=0
  notify.log: === notify-capture exiting at 2026-08-23T13:11:50,379503503+02:00 with rc=0 ===

Sequential, not concurrent: our own work (receipt + queue call, ~355ms,
dominated by the `codex queue` subprocess spawn/round-trip) completed before
the foreign program ran (~3ms). Total wrapper wall time end-to-end (receipt
to exit) was ~375ms, well inside a 10s hook-style timeout budget. The
foreign program received the exact same single JSON argv[1] payload the
wrapper itself received (argv preserved).
